Welcome to a journey where we look beyond the surface of poverty and ask ourselves—what does it really mean to help?
You know, so many of us are moved by the urge to make a difference, yet sometimes, even the best intentions can bring about challenges we never expected.
That’s exactly the kind of honest exploration Steve Corbett offers in his thoughtful book, When Helping Hurts: How to Alleviate Poverty Without Hurting the Poor . . . and Yourself.
Together, we’ll dive into stories and insights that reveal how true change isn’t just about handing out resources—it’s about understanding the bigger picture, the systems at play, and the unique dignity of every person involved.
Ever wonder why some well-meaning efforts end up reinforcing dependency or even holding back local potential? This is where we’ll start asking the tough questions, and looking for answers that lead to real empowerment and lasting change.
As we explore the practical frameworks and real-world examples woven throughout this narrative, you’ll find that the heart of genuine transformation lies in partnership, humility, and a willingness to learn from one another.
So, let’s step forward together—ready to rethink what it means to help, and eager to discover how every act of kindness can honor the strengths, hopes, and dreams of those we serve, as well as our own.
